narration.say: Kicked flat. How does it get up?
In a new study, researchers kicked this robot 47 times.
To stand, its center of mass must be over its feet.

narration.say: So it plants its hands, shifts its weight over its feet, then lets go.

narration.say: On the real robot: 34 falls, 34 get-ups.

shots.beat: first frame / hook: a humanoid kicked flat on a paper test lawn, pushing up; centre-of-mass marker + plumb line; "KICKED FLAT. / HOW DOES IT GET UP?"
the study: the robot stands, a boot kicks it from behind, it falls forward (prone); "47 kicks" counter + dated chip
principle: centre of mass far from the feet (red); a ghost standing over its feet shows the goal
mechanism: plants hands (wide support), steps feet in, shifts weight back; hand force falls to 0 N, lets go, stands (live statics readout)
training trick: in a simulation grid world a 400 N lift on the head helps, then fades to 0 N (20 N steps)
hardware result: 47 tiles; 34 falls flip to get-ups; 5 no-fall + 8 safety cut-outs; stopwatch 2.64 s mean
payoff: the robot walks on (task resumed); a kick-force meter reads "?" — proves recovery, not toughness
CTA: Media Diet sign flips up; the robot waves behind it
